# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Barbolosi_2017_radioiodine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Barbolosi_2017_radioiodine"))$description`
* Model development article (Barbolosi 2017, Oncotarget): <https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.16637>
* Protocol-simulation article (Fusella Giuntini 2026, Scientific Reports): <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-56267-1>
* Authors' MATLAB simulator (RAIR-Sim): <https://github.com/MarieFG49/CTD_SIMU_RAI>

Barbolosi 2017 built and fitted the model (Monolix, SAEM) to stimulated
serum thyroglobulin (Tg) from 50 patients with lung-metastatic papillary
thyroid carcinoma. Fusella Giuntini 2026 reused the same population
estimates, without re-estimation, to study how the number of iodine-131
courses `n`, the interval between them `Delta t` and the activity per course
`A` change the predicted Tg course in responders and non-responders, and
released the MATLAB simulator that does so. This article packages the model
once and reproduces the protocol figures of the 2026 paper.

The model has three states, with time in months:

* `activity` (GBq): the *effective* radioiodine activity. Each course is a
  bolus of the administered activity; it is lost at `a * ln(2)` per month,
  much more slowly than the 8-day physical half-life of iodine-131, because
  it represents the delayed cell-killing effect.
* `tumor` (cells): exponential growth with doubling time `Td` under
  treatment, killed at rate `rho * A(t)`.
* `thyroglobulin` (ng/mL): produced at `lambda` per tumor cell and
  eliminated at `ke`; the observed output.

A two-class Monolix mixture on `Td` separates non-responders (`Td` = 9.8
months, 27.5%) from responders (`Td` = 66.6 months, 72.5%). The class is the
covariate `MIX_FAST_GROW` (1 = non-responder).

# Population

Barbolosi 2017 (Results, "Patient characteristics"; Materials and methods)
included 50 patients from eight French institutions, aged 8-55 years (mean
29), with papillary thyroid carcinoma and diffuse lung metastases (all M1;
pT1/pT2 7, pT3/pT4 43; N1 47, Nx 3). All had total thyroidectomy, with
lymph-node dissection except in 3. Patients received iodine-131 at
3.7-5.5 GBq per course (one 8-year-old received 1.85 GBq for the first
course), usually every 6-8 months, with endogenous TSH stimulation, at least
3 courses and at least 3 years of follow-up; the mean cumulative activity was
22.2 GBq. Stimulated Tg was measured before each course. The sex distribution
is not reported. Fusella Giuntini 2026 Appendix B describes the same cohort.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `dA/dt = -a ln(2) A` | -- | Barbolosi 2017 Materials and methods; RAIR-Sim `Demonstrateur98f.m` (`diff(A) == -a*log(2)*A`) |
| `dN/dt = ln(2)/Td N - rho A N`, `N(0) = N0` | -- | Barbolosi 2017 Materials and methods; Fusella Giuntini 2026 Eq. 1b |
| `dTg/dt = -ke Tg + lambda N`, `Tg(0) = Tg0` | -- | Barbolosi 2017 Materials and methods; Fusella Giuntini 2026 Eq. 1c |
| Course = bolus into `A`, `A(0) = 0` | -- | Fusella Giuntini 2026 "The compartmental model"; RAIR-Sim `A00 = 0` |
| `a` (`lkdecay`, fixed) | 0.0169 /month | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1; Fusella Giuntini 2026 Table 1 |
| `rho` (`lkkill`, fixed) | 0.00407 /(GBq month) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1; Fusella Giuntini 2026 Table 1 |
| `lambda` (`lksyn`, fixed) | 3.86e-9 ng/mL/month per cell | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1; Fusella Giuntini 2026 Table 1 |
| `ke` (`lkdeg`) | 0.319 /month | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| `N0` (`lrbase_tumor`) | 1.12e9 cells | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| `Td`, non-responder (`ltdouble_pop1`) | 9.8 months | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 'Td cat=1' |
| `Td`, responder (`ltdouble_pop2`) | 66.6 months | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 'Td cat=2' |
| Class probability, non-responder | 0.275 | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 'pi cat1' |
| `Tg0` (`lrbase_thyroglobulin`, fixed) | 100 ng/mL | Fusella Giuntini 2026 "Practical implementation" |
| IIV SD on `ke` (`etalkdeg`) | 1.16 (variance 1.3456) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| IIV SD on `lambda` (`etalksyn`) | 2.47 (variance 6.1009) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| IIV SD on `Td` (`etaltdouble`, fixed) | 0.3 (variance 0.09) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| IIV SD on `N0` | 2.05e-7 (numerically zero; no eta) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| IIV on `rho`, `a` | 0 (no eta) | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |
| Proportional residual SD `b` (`propSd`) | 0.372 | Barbolosi 2017 Table 1 |

# Typical-value protocol simulations

All of the 2026 paper's simulations use typical values (no between-subject
variability), `Tg0` = 100 ng/mL, the first course at time 0 and later courses
every `Delta t` months, read out to 80 months. Because `Tg0` is 100, the
y axis of the published figures ("Tg(t) (Unitless)") is both ng/mL and
percent of baseline.

```{r protocol-helpers}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Barbolosi_2017_radioiodine"))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value solve of a multi-subject event table. rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject simulation has no omega, which is the intent here; only that
# message is muffled.
solve_typ <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, ...)),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

obs_times <- seq(0, 80, by = 0.25)

# One subject's event table for n courses of `act` GBq every `lag` months.
protocol_events <- function(id, n, lag, act, mix) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = (seq_len(n) - 1) * lag, amt = act, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "activity"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "thyroglobulin"
  )
  out <- rbind(doses, obs)
  out$MIX_FAST_GROW <- mix
  out
}

# The three one-at-a-time sweeps of Figures 2 and 3: (a) n = 1..8,
# (b) Delta t = 1..8 months with n = 8, (c) A = 1..8 GBq with n = 8.
protocol_sweep <- function(mix, lag_default) {
  sweeps <- list(
    a = lapply(1:8, function(i) {
      transform(protocol_events(i, i, lag_default, 3.7, mix), panel = "a", value = i)
    }),
    b = lapply(1:8, function(i) {
      transform(protocol_events(100 + i, 8, i, 3.7, mix), panel = "b", value = i)
    }),
    c = lapply(1:8, function(i) {
      transform(protocol_events(200 + i, 8, lag_default, i, mix), panel = "c", value = i)
    })
  )
  ev <- do.call(rbind, unlist(sweeps, recursive = FALSE))
  solve_typ(ev, keep = c("panel", "value"))
}

panel_labels <- c(
  a = "(a) n = 1..8 courses",
  b = "(b) interval = 1..8 months, n = 8",
  c = "(c) activity = 1..8 GBq, n = 8"
)

plot_sweep <- function(sim) {
  ggplot(sim, aes(time, thyroglobulin, colour = factor(value), group = factor(value))) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~panel, labeller = as_labeller(panel_labels)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "n / months / GBq") +
    labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Tg (ng/mL = % of baseline)")
}

tg_at <- function(sim, pnl, val, t) {
  sim$thyroglobulin[sim$panel == pnl & sim$value == val & abs(sim$time - t) < 1e-8]
}
```

## Non-responders (`Td` = 9.8 months)

```{r fig2, fig.height = 3.5}
sim_nr <- protocol_sweep(mix = 1, lag_default = 3)
plot_sweep(sim_nr) +
  ggtitle("Non-responder: A = 3.7 GBq, interval 3 months unless varied")
```

Replicates Figure 2 of Fusella Giuntini 2026. The checks below restate the
2026 Results text ("Influence of protocol parameters for patients with
Td = 9.8 months") and points read off the figure:

```{r fig2-checks}
stopifnot(
  # (a) n = 7 or 8: "decreases and stabilizes between Tg(10%) and Tg(20%)".
  all(sapply(7:8, function(n) {
    x <- tg_at(sim_nr, "a", n, 60)
    x > 10 && x < 20
  })),
  # (a) a single course: Tg crosses 100 ng/mL near 40 months in the figure.
  tg_at(sim_nr, "a", 1, 35) < 100, tg_at(sim_nr, "a", 1, 45) > 100,
  # (b) interval 8 months: peak near 50 ng/mL at about 50 months, ~40 at 80.
  abs(max(sim_nr$thyroglobulin[sim_nr$panel == "b" & sim_nr$value == 8 &
    sim_nr$time > 20]) - 50) < 3,
  abs(tg_at(sim_nr, "b", 8, 80) - 40) < 3,
  # (c) 3 GBq: "remains stable between Tg(20%) and Tg(24%) up to 60 months".
  all(sim_nr$thyroglobulin[sim_nr$panel == "c" & sim_nr$value == 3 &
    sim_nr$time >= 15 & sim_nr$time <= 60] < 24.5),
  all(sim_nr$thyroglobulin[sim_nr$panel == "c" & sim_nr$value == 3 &
    sim_nr$time >= 15 & sim_nr$time <= 60] > 19.5),
  # (c) "below Tg(10%) at 18 months for 8 GBq and around 40 months for 4 GBq".
  abs(tg_at(sim_nr, "c", 8, 18) - 10) < 1,
  abs(tg_at(sim_nr, "c", 4, 40) - 10) < 1
)
```

## Responders (`Td` = 66.6 months)

```{r fig3, fig.height = 3.5}
sim_r <- protocol_sweep(mix = 0, lag_default = 6)
plot_sweep(sim_r) +
  ggtitle("Responder: A = 3.7 GBq, interval 6 months unless varied")
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Fusella Giuntini 2026 (whose sweeps (a) and (c) use a
6-month interval, per the authors' `main_demonstrateur666f.m`). The checks
restate the Results text for `Td` = 66.6 months:

```{r fig3-checks}
stopifnot(
  # (a) n = 1: "stabilizes at Tg(14%)"; the figure plateaus at 13-14.
  all(sim_r$thyroglobulin[sim_r$panel == "a" & sim_r$value == 1 &
    sim_r$time >= 20] > 12),
  all(sim_r$thyroglobulin[sim_r$panel == "a" & sim_r$value == 1 &
    sim_r$time >= 20] < 15),
  # (a) n = 2..8: below Tg(10%) between 20 and 30 months, below 8% at 50.
  all(sapply(2:8, function(n) tg_at(sim_r, "a", n, 30) < 10)),
  all(sapply(2:8, function(n) tg_at(sim_r, "a", n, 50) < 8)),
  # (c) below Tg(10%) at about 15 months for 8 GBq and 60 months for 1 GBq.
  abs(tg_at(sim_r, "c", 8, 15) - 10) < 1,
  abs(tg_at(sim_r, "c", 1, 60) - 10) < 1
)
```

## Simulator examples (Figures 4 and 5)

```{r fig45}
examples <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  label = c(
    "Fig 4b: non-responder, 5 x 3.7 GBq q6mo",
    "Fig 4d: non-responder, 5 x 5.55 GBq q6mo",
    "Fig 5b: responder, 5 x 1.85 GBq q6mo",
    "Fig 5d: responder, 3 x 1.85 GBq q6mo"
  ),
  n = c(5, 5, 5, 3), act = c(3.7, 5.55, 1.85, 1.85), mix = c(1, 1, 0, 0)
)
ev_ex <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(examples)), function(i) {
  with(examples[i, ], protocol_events(id, n, 6, act, mix))
}))
sim_ex <- solve_typ(ev_ex) |>
  left_join(examples[, c("id", "label")], by = "id") |>
  filter(time <= 60)

ggplot(sim_ex, aes(time, thyroglobulin)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Tg (ng/mL)")

ex_at <- function(i, t) sim_ex$thyroglobulin[sim_ex$id == i & abs(sim_ex$time - t) < 1e-8]
stopifnot(
  # Fig 4b: minimum about 23 ng/mL at 10 months, about 56 ng/mL at 60 months.
  abs(ex_at(1, 10) - 23) < 2, abs(ex_at(1, 60) - 56) < 3,
  # Fig 4d: falling after 25 months, about 15 ng/mL at 60 months.
  ex_at(2, 40) < ex_at(2, 25), abs(ex_at(2, 60) - 15) < 2
)
```

Replicates Figures 4(b, d) and 5(b, d) of Fusella Giuntini 2026: raising the
activity to 5.55 GBq turns a rising non-responder Tg course into a falling
one, and a responder keeps a falling course with 3 instead of 5 courses.

# Solver check against the closed form

With constant parameters the model has a closed form between courses, which
is how RAIR-Sim solves it. With `k = a ln(2)`, the effective activity is
`A(t) = sum_k A_k exp(-k (t - t_k))` over past courses, the tumor is
`N(t) = N0 exp(ln(2) t / Td - rho * integral_0^t A)`, and
`Tg(t) = Tg0 exp(-ke t) + lambda * integral_0^t N(s) exp(-ke (t - s)) ds`.
The last integral is evaluated numerically below and compared with the ODE
solution for the non-responder 8-course protocol.

```{r closed-form}
p <- list(
  k = 0.0169 * log(2), rho = 0.00407, lambda = 3.86e-9, ke = 0.319,
  n0 = 1.12e9, tg0 = 100, kgrow = log(2) / 9.8
)
dose_t <- (0:7) * 3
dose_a <- rep(3.7, 8)
int_a <- function(t) {
  sapply(t, function(tt) {
    on <- dose_t <= tt
    sum(dose_a[on] / p$k * (1 - exp(-p$k * (tt - dose_t[on]))))
  })
}
n_cf <- function(t) p$n0 * exp(p$kgrow * t - p$rho * int_a(t))
tg_cf <- function(t) {
  p$tg0 * exp(-p$ke * t) +
    p$lambda * integrate(function(s) n_cf(s) * exp(-p$ke * (t - s)), 0, t,
      rel.tol = 1e-10, subdivisions = 1000L
    )$value
}
chk_t <- c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80)
cf <- data.frame(
  time = chk_t,
  closed_form = sapply(chk_t, tg_cf),
  ode = sapply(chk_t, function(t) tg_at(sim_nr, "a", 8, t))
) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = ode / closed_form - 1)
knitr::kable(cf, digits = 6)
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is numerical error only.
stopifnot(all(abs(cf$rel_diff) < 1e-4))
```

# Between-subject variability and the mixture

The population model adds log-normal IIV on `ke`, `lambda` and `Td`, a
proportional residual error, and the mixture class. The simulation below
draws 200 virtual patients with `MIX_FAST_GROW ~ Bernoulli(0.275)`, each
treated with 6 courses of 3.7 GBq every 6 months (22.2 GBq cumulative, the
cohort mean), with `Tg0` = 100 ng/mL. Measured `Tg0` varies between patients;
to use it, add a `lrbase_thyroglobulin = log(Tg0)` column to the data.

```{r vpc}
set.seed(2017)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2017)
n_sub <- 200
mix <- rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.275)
ev_pop <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  protocol_events(i, 6, 6, 3.7, mix[i])
}))
ev_pop <- ev_pop[ev_pop$evid == 1 | ev_pop$time %in% seq(0, 60, by = 2), ]
sim_pop <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pop, keep = "MIX_FAST_GROW")) |>
  mutate(class = ifelse(MIX_FAST_GROW == 1, "Non-responder (Td 9.8 mo)", "Responder (Td 66.6 mo)"))

sim_pop |>
  group_by(class, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(thyroglobulin, 0.05), q50 = median(thyroglobulin),
    q95 = quantile(thyroglobulin, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~class) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (months)", y = "Tg (ng/mL, 5th-50th-95th percentiles)")
```

The wide band reflects the large IIV on `lambda` (SD 2.47 on the log scale),
which carries most of the between-patient spread in Tg level. The median
course differs between the classes in the direction the mixture defines:

```{r vpc-check}
med48 <- sim_pop |>
  filter(time == 48) |>
  group_by(MIX_FAST_GROW) |>
  summarise(median_tg = median(thyroglobulin), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(med48, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  med48$median_tg[med48$MIX_FAST_GROW == 1] > med48$median_tg[med48$MIX_FAST_GROW == 0]
)
```

# NCA

This is a tumor and biomarker model driven by a delayed-effect activity
state, not a drug-concentration model, so non-compartmental analysis does not
apply. Neither paper reports NCA. Validation is by reproducing the published
simulations and by the closed-form check above.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **The model comes from Barbolosi 2017; the protocol simulations from
  Fusella Giuntini 2026.** The 2026 paper re-prints the Barbolosi 2017
  estimates (its Appendix A Table 1) and does not re-fit the model, so one
  model file carries both citations. Residual error, the mixture
  probabilities and the S.E.s are taken from Barbolosi 2017 Table 1, which
  the 2026 table does not reproduce.
* **`ln(2)` in the activity equation.** Fusella Giuntini 2026 Eq. (1a) prints
  `dA/dt = -a A`. Barbolosi 2017 and the authors' MATLAB code
  (`diff(A) == -a*log(2)*A`) both include the `ln(2)`, and the published
  figures are reproduced only with it, so the model follows the code.
* **`Td` in the 2026 Table 1 is a typographical error.** Fusella Giuntini
  2026 Table 1 prints a mean `Td` of 9.98 months; Barbolosi 2017 Table 1, the
  2026 text and the MATLAB code all use 9.8 months for the non-responder
  class and 66.6 months for responders. The model uses 9.8 and 66.6.
* **The 'Std' row of the 2026 Table 1 is the IIV.** Its values (`N0` and the
  fixed parameters `< 1e-3`, `Td` 0.3, `lambda` 2.47, `ke` 1.16) are the
  Monolix IIV standard deviations of Barbolosi 2017 Table 1, not standard
  errors. Monolix reports omega as the SD of the log-normal random effect, so
  the variances are their squares.
* **Fixed or estimated.** Barbolosi 2017 states that `rho`, `a` and `lambda`
  were fixed after showing little variability; they carry `fixed()`. The `Td`
  IIV is printed without an S.E. and is also encoded as fixed. The `N0` IIV
  SD of 2.05e-7 (no S.E.) is numerically zero and is omitted: as a variance of
  4e-14 it adds nothing to a simulation and makes rxode2 rewrite the omega
  matrix with a warning.
* **Mixture parameterisation.** Monolix estimated `Td` for category 1 (9.8
  months) and a category-2 effect `beta_Td` = 1.92; the model uses the two
  printed group values directly (9.8 and 66.6 months; `9.8 exp(1.92)` =
  66.9). The `Td` IIV is shared by both classes.
* **`Tg0`.** In Barbolosi 2017, `Tg(0)` is each patient's first stimulated
  Tg before treatment, so it is data rather than an estimated parameter. The
  model fixes it at the 100 ng/mL used for every 2026 simulation; supply
  `lrbase_thyroglobulin` per subject to use measured values. `Tg0` is not at
  the steady state implied by `N0` (`lambda N0 / ke` = 13.6 ng/mL), which is
  why every simulated course falls steeply over the first months.
* **Responder fraction.** Barbolosi 2017 reports 80% clinically classified
  responders; the mixture assigned 72.5% to the responder class. Fusella
  Giuntini 2026 Appendix B gives "~70%" and 72.5%. The model uses the mixture
  probability.
* **Text versus figure in the 2026 Results.** Two statements in the 2026 text
  do not match its own Figure 2: the 1-month interval reaches about 6%, not
  8-12%, at 50-60 months, and the 4-month interval peaks near 24% rather than
  having a minimum near 20%. The packaged model reproduces the figure, which
  was generated by the published code, so the checks above follow the figure.
